glossary.Fracture risk: The chance of breaking a bone, usually expressed over the next 10 years.
glossary.White ethnicity: People of European descent, who have a higher risk of osteoporosis.
glossary.Postmenopausal: After the menopause, when ovarian oestrogen production has stopped.
glossary.Steroids: Corticosteroid drugs such as prednisolone; long-term use thins bone.
glossary.RA: Rheumatoid arthritis, an autoimmune joint disease that raises osteoporosis risk and is an input to FRAX.
glossary.Sedentary: Physically inactive, with little weight-bearing exercise.
glossary.Low-impact fall: A fall from standing height or less.
glossary.Hip fracture: A break at the top of the femur, usually after a fall; carries high morbidity and mortality.
glossary.Vertebrae: The bones that make up the spine.
glossary.Gender: Whether the patient is male or female; DEXA reference values are adjusted for it.
glossary.Reference population: Healthy young adults whose average bone density the T score is compared with.
glossary.Major osteoporotic fracture: Fracture of the hip, spine, wrist or upper arm.
glossary.Intermediate risk: A FRAX fracture risk high enough to need a DEXA scan before deciding on treatment.
glossary.Testosterone: The main male sex hormone; low levels thin bone, so it is checked in men.
glossary.Contraindicated: Should not be given because the harm is likely to outweigh the benefit.
glossary.Oesophagitis: Inflammation of the oesophagus, a side effect of oral bisphosphonates.
glossary.Peptic ulceration: Open sores in the stomach or duodenal lining.
glossary.Dyspepsia: Indigestion: upper abdominal discomfort, often after eating.
glossary.Reflux: Stomach acid coming back up into the oesophagus, causing heartburn.
glossary.Weight-bearing exercise: Exercise on your feet, such as walking, which loads bone and helps keep it strong.
glossary.Falls prevention: Measures that cut the chance of falling, such as removing hazards, reviewing drugs and improving balance.
glossary.Subcutaneously: Injected into the fat just under the skin.
glossary.Monoclonal antibody: A lab-made antibody that binds one specific target molecule.
glossary.RANK: A receptor on osteoclast precursors; when RANKL binds it, osteoclasts form and resorb bone.
glossary.Apoptosis: Programmed cell death, a controlled way for a cell to die.
glossary.Resorption: Breakdown of bone by osteoclasts, releasing minerals into the blood.
glossary.Microarchitecture: The fine internal structure of bone, the network of trabeculae.
glossary.Oestrogen deficiency: Low oestrogen, as after menopause, which removes a brake on osteoclasts.
glossary.Morbidity: Illness, disability or loss of function caused by a disease.
glossary.Mineralisation: Laying down calcium and phosphate crystals in the bone matrix; normal in osteoporosis.
